newsitem.title: USA: Entergy has extensive damage to Ark. lines.
newsitem.headline: Entergy has extensive damage to Ark. lines.

text.p: Entergy Corp said Monday it would likely take up to three weeks to repair Arkansas power transmission lines downed this past weekend by tornadoes.
"The damage to our distribution system is far more dramatic than the number of customer ouatges," said Carol Copeland, spokeswoman Entergy's Little Rock office.
"Thirty-six of our steel transmission towers were either damaged or detroyed...It will take anywhere from two to three days to two to three weeks to rebuild some of the towers," she said.

About 2,700 Entergy customers are currently without power, a sharp drop from the 18,000 left in the dark when a band of some 20 tornadoes swept across Arkansas Saturday night, killing at least 24 people and injuring up to 200.
Entergy, headquartered in New Orleans, Louisiana, has about 611,000 customers in Arkansas.
Copeland said Entergy's power plants were not hurt by the severe waether and that the company was not purchasing power in the spot market.
"We are backfeeding power to our customers on other lines, so the number of people without power is relatively small," she said.

"Most of the outages are in southwest Little Rock and Newport, northeast of Little Rock. But in the worst-hit areas, like Arkedelphia, not a lot of buildings can receive power. The downtown area there was flattened," she said.

Entergy's Arkansas 1 nuclear power plant in Russellville, Ark., reduced power output to 53 percent of its rated 836 megawatt capacity due to the loss of transmission lines in the region, the Nuclear Regulatory Commission reported earlier Monday.
